title: Skeleton Enterprise System Architecture
purpose: Define the system-of-systems contract that turns Skeleton's existing runtime, AI construction, state, security, reliability, release, and operator planes into one operable enterprise platform.

compatibility.rule: This contract is additive. It composes existing authorities and may not create a shadow state owner, provider runtime, tool executor, policy engine, or conversation authority.

system_outcomes: one deployable product with explicit runtime and control-plane topology
one authority for every canonical state domain and one contract for every cross-plane dependency
tenant-safe execution with least privilege, bounded side effects, durable lineage, and auditable decisions
horizontal application and engine scaling without duplicate canonical writes
degraded operation that is explicit, bounded, and never fabricates success
measurable SLOs with release promotion and rollback driven by current evidence
recoverability from process, node, provider, database, region, and operator failure
repeatable deployment, backup, restore, incident response, and change management
compliance-ready data lifecycle controls without claiming unearned certification
machine-verifiable architecture evidence at exact repository head
invariants: production authority is explicit and singular for every canonical state domain
client state, cache state, vector state, telemetry, and streamed output are never promoted to canonical authority
all service-to-service mutations are authenticated, authorized, idempotent where replay is possible, and traceable
model output is never authorization and cannot directly acquire privileged tool or repository authority
provider, tool, memory, retrieval, artifact, conversation, release, and governance receipts preserve operation lineage
tenant scope is mandatory at every canonical state, retrieval, memory, artifact, and tool boundary
security and governance dependency failure is fail-closed for protected actions
capacity exhaustion sheds, defers, or degrades work before canonical consistency is sacrificed
derived stores are rebuildable from canonical state or are explicitly marked non-rebuildable with recovery ownership
production readiness is an evidence state, never a documentation label
rollback preserves canonical state compatibility or includes a tested forward-fix/migration path
observability may degrade but canonical writes never depend on telemetry availability
deployment technology is replaceable; authority, state, recovery, security, and SLO semantics are not
no production single point of failure is accepted without an explicit approved exception and expiry

runtime_cell.topology: three stateless request-serving tiers over canonical durable state, with optional derived retrieval state

ingress.rule: production ingress terminates TLS, applies request bounds and identity policy, and never exposes database ports publicly

service_identity.target: short-lived workload identity with mutually authenticated service calls for protected internal mutation paths
service_identity.transitional: signed delegated authority and authenticated engine boundary remain valid while mTLS/workload identity is introduced
service_identity.credential_rule: static shared credentials are prohibited for new production service-to-service trust

deployment_profiles.purpose: production-like integration, migrations, canary rehearsal and restore drills

deployment_profiles.orchestrator: vendor-neutral scheduler with health-aware rolling deployment
requirements: multiple failure domains for tier-0 and tier-1 services
durable replica/quorum semantics for canonical state
rolling or canary deployment with automatic rollback
encrypted backup and point-in-time recovery for authoritative stores
independent health, readiness and dependency-safe admission
central audit, metrics, traces and alert routing

owns: authorized evidence retrieval and derived indexes
governed learning proposals and promotion evidence

tenancy.model: shared platform with mandatory logical tenant isolation; dedicated deployments remain an optional stronger isolation profile
tenancy.authorization: RBAC for coarse role plus attribute/policy checks for tenant, resource, capability, data class, action risk and approval state
isolation_requirements: tenant filter applied before retrieval ranking
tenant and owner binding at canonical repositories
artifact object keys and lifecycle records tenant-bound
tool grants and provider delegated authority tenant-bound
audit events preserve tenant and acting principal without logging secrets or raw restricted payloads

privileged_access.production_admin: just-in-time, short-lived, auditable and separated from ordinary user credentials
privileged_access.break_glass: explicit reason, strong authentication, bounded expiry, immutable audit and post-incident review
privileged_access.service_accounts: non-human identities with minimum scopes and rotation

rules: classification is preserved or made more restrictive across derived artifacts
provider routing enforces data-class privacy ceilings before network egress
retention, export, deletion and legal-hold policy act on canonical authorities first and projections second
restricted payloads are excluded from default logs, metrics labels, traces and crash reports
backup copies inherit retention, encryption, deletion and access-control obligations

security_architecture.model: zero-trust-by-boundary, deny-by-default for protected mutation and external transfer

cryptography.in_transit: TLS 1.2+; TLS 1.3 preferred; protected internal production mutations target mutually authenticated transport
cryptography.at_rest: encryption required for canonical databases, backups and artifact storage
cryptography.key_management: centrally managed keys with environment separation, rotation, access audit and no repository-stored production secrets

vulnerability_response.critical: triage immediately; mitigation or containment target within 24 hours
vulnerability_response.rule: active exploitation or tenant-boundary failure overrides ordinary severity timing

reliability.philosophy: prefer explicit bounded degradation over hidden fallback; preserve canonical state before optional capability
patterns: bounded retries with jitter only for retry-safe operations
circuit breaking around providers and remote dependencies
idempotency and fencing for replayable mutation paths
bulkheads for tenants, providers and expensive work classes
graceful shutdown with admission stop and bounded drain
automatic rollback on failed canary evidence

service_level_objectives.measurement_rule: No SLO is considered achieved until the production telemetry window and evidence receipt satisfy its definition.

objectives.scope: authenticated backend and engine request admission excluding declared maintenance
request validation/admission before provider model execution
first durable progress/stream status for admitted interactive AI work

objectives.target: 99.99% accepted privileged actions produce audit evidence
100% scheduled drills complete within declared RTO

tiers.rpo: 0 for acknowledged commits inside the active replicated region; <= 5m for region-loss recovery target

tiers.class: tier-1 durable artifacts and release evidence

backup_requirements: encrypted backups with separate failure-domain custody
point-in-time recovery for canonical database where supported
restore into isolated environment before promotion
quarterly restore drill and annual region-loss exercise
backup success without restore proof does not satisfy DR evidence

controls: queue depth, age and shed thresholds
token, cost, storage and external-write budgets
large-project workloads isolated from interactive latency pools
autoscaling based on admitted work and saturation rather than raw request count alone
overload_order: shed optional enrichment/retrieval where policy permits
never drop already acknowledged canonical writes

telemetry: USE metrics for compute, queue and store saturation
provider latency/error/quality/cost by non-secret provider identity
retrieval freshness/quality and citation verification metrics
release canary SLO and rollback state
observability_and_sre.logging_rule: structured logs are content-minimized by default; raw prompts, secrets, restricted payloads and full tool results require explicitly governed diagnostics

requirements: post-incident corrective actions with owner and due date

principles: every production change has immutable source revision and build provenance
database/schema changes are expand-migrate-contract with compatibility window
feature flags reduce release coupling but are not permanent alternate architectures
canary or progressive delivery precedes full production rollout for material risk
rollback is automated when SLO or integrity evidence fails
security and authority regressions are non-overridable promotion blockers
promotion_evidence: AI construction, capability-interface, state-topology and app-assembly validators
security, dependency, malware and provenance gates
migration preflight and backward-compatibility evidence when state changes
load/capacity evidence for changed hot paths

roles.accountable_for: runtime health, backlog, SLO and runbooks
authority boundaries, dependency direction and contract evolution
threat model, incident containment and security exceptions
classification, lifecycle, privacy and deletion/export controls

review_cadence.daily: automated SLO/error-budget and security signal review
review_cadence.weekly: operating review for incidents, capacity, backlog and degraded dependencies
review_cadence.monthly: SLO/error-budget, dependency, access and restore-freshness review
review_cadence.quarterly: restore drill, threat-model review, failover/game-day and architecture debt review
review_cadence.annual: region-loss exercise and enterprise control-baseline review

required_journeys: authenticate -> create conversation -> multi-turn AI response -> durable reconstruction
retrieval-backed answer -> evidence/citation verification -> accepted response
tool proposal -> approval when required -> exactly-once side effect -> durable receipt
artifact upload -> scan -> parse/use -> lifecycle -> export/delete
provider outage -> compliant failover or explicit degraded response
engine restart -> durable operation resume -> canonical completion
client disconnect -> stream/poll resume without duplicate completion
tenant export/delete -> cross-plane propagation -> physical lifecycle acknowledgement
overload -> fair shedding/defer -> preserved canonical writes
bad release -> canary SLO breach -> automatic rollback -> preserved data compatibility
backup restore -> isolated validation -> service reconstruction -> derived index rebuild
privileged operator action -> JIT authority -> immutable audit -> expiry

architecture_plan_complete_requires: enterprise contract parses and cross-links every canonical source
all enterprise domains are mapped to declared AI capability planes
runtime cell exactly matches the application manifest services
SLO, DR, security, tenancy, capacity, observability, release and operating-model sections pass structural validation
machine validator and independent verifier are exact-head capable
workflow runs the enterprise validator plus existing architecture/construction/state validators
production_ready_requires: all production-ha requirements evidenced in a production-like environment
all required journeys green at exact release head
current SLO window satisfies release policy
no open unexpired tier-0 architecture/security exception
capacity/load evidence for declared production envelope
evidence_model.signoff_rule: plan_complete may be true when architecture-plan evidence is complete; production_claim must remain false until every production_ready_requires item is independently evidenced.

implementation_workstreams.name: Runtime cell and service identity
exit: all production service calls have declared identity/authn path

implementation_workstreams.name: SLO/SLI and error-budget plane
exit: all enterprise SLOs have live measurements
release controller consumes same SLO source

implementation_workstreams.name: Service-to-service zero trust
exit: protected internal mTLS or equivalent authenticated channel

implementation_workstreams.name: Compliance-ready control evidence
exit: jurisdiction-specific overlays can be enabled without architecture fork
